==== TOOL mailpiece_identity ====
title: Mailpiece Identity
Who you are on Mailpiece, a newsletter app where one account is one newsletter: the accounts (newsletters) your token can reach and your user and role in each. Call this first to learn which newsletter you are working in.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- get_identity (RO): List the accounts the token can reach, with your user in each
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "get_identity",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
---- describe get_identity ----
{
  "action": "get_identity",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/my/identity",
  "summary": "List the accounts the token can reach, with your user in each",
  "doc": "Each account carries a slug naming it in API paths: always its number. A handle also answers in a path but changes, so configuration keeps the number. The other tools run against the account the server is configured for; this action shows every account the token can reach.",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false,
  "unscoped": true
}
==== TOOL mailpiece_access_tokens ====
title: Mailpiece Access Tokens
Mailpiece access tokens: the signed-in person's personal access tokens, which let a program such as this one act as them. A token is read or write; read allows looking only.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- create_access_token: Create an access token for the signed-in person. The token is in the response once and never again.
- delete_access_token (destructive): Delete one of the signed-in person's access tokens; whatever uses it stops working. This cannot be undone.
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "create_access_token",
        "delete_access_token",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
---- describe create_access_token ----
{
  "action": "create_access_token",
  "method": "POST",
  "path": "/my/access_tokens",
  "summary": "Create an access token for the signed-in person. The token is in the response once and never again.",
  "readonly": false,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false,
  "body": {
    "properties": {
      "description": {
        "description": "What the token is for",
        "type": "string"
      },
      "permission": {
        "description": "read (looking only) or write",
        "enum": [
          "read",
          "write"
        ],
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": [
      "description",
      "permission"
    ],
    "type": "object"
  },
  "body_key": "access_token",
  "unscoped": true
}
---- describe delete_access_token ----
{
  "action": "delete_access_token",
  "method": "DELETE",
  "path": "/my/access_tokens/{access_token_id}",
  "summary": "Delete one of the signed-in person's access tokens; whatever uses it stops working. This cannot be undone.",
  "readonly": false,
  "idempotent": true,
  "destructive": true,
  "params": [
    {
      "name": "access_token_id",
      "in": "path",
      "required": true,
      "description": "The access token's ID (from its create)",
      "schema": {
        "description": "The access token's ID (from its create)",
        "type": "string"
      }
    }
  ],
  "unscoped": true
}
==== TOOL mailpiece_snippets ====
title: Mailpiece Snippets
Mailpiece snippets: named pieces of rich text a newsletter keeps and pastes into its posts. A snippet is pasted as ordinary text, so changing or deleting one never changes a post already written. Admins only.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- create_snippet: Add a snippet
- delete_snippet (destructive): Delete a snippet for good. This cannot be undone.
- get_snippet (RO): Get a snippet
- list_snippets (RO): List every snippet, by name, each with its content
- update_snippet: Change a snippet's name or content; only what is passed changes
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "create_snippet",
        "delete_snippet",
        "get_snippet",
        "list_snippets",
        "update_snippet",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

  "readonly": false,

  "destructive": false,
  "body": {
    "properties": {
      "content": {
        "description": "Content, as HTML",
        "type": "string"
      },
      "name": {
        "description": "Snippet name",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "required": [
      "name"
    ],
    "type": "object"

==== TOOL mailpiece_journeys ====
title: Mailpiece Journeys
Mailpiece journeys: the emails a newsletter mails by itself to a person after they confirm their subscription (subscriber_confirmed, each email after its own delay) or after they unsubscribe (subscriber_unsubscribed, one email, at once). A journey is known by its trigger and always exists. An email is a draft until activated. Admins only.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- activate_journey_email (destructive): Switch an email on: from then on it is mailed by itself to real people as they reach it, until it is switched off; mail that has gone out stays sent. This cannot be undone.
- create_journey_email: Add an email to a journey, as a draft mailed to nobody until activated
- deactivate_journey_email: Switch an email off: it is a draft again and is mailed to nobody
- delete_journey_email (destructive): Delete an email of a journey for good, active or not. This cannot be undone.
- get_journey (RO): Get a journey with its emails in full
- get_journey_email (RO): Get one email of a journey in full, active or not
- list_journeys (RO): List every journey, each with its emails in full
- test_journey_email (destructive): Mail one test copy of an email, active or not, to an address or to the signed-in person's own. It is real mail. This cannot be undone.
- update_journey_email: Change an email of a journey; only what is passed changes
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "activate_journey_email",
        "create_journey_email",
        "deactivate_journey_email",
        "delete_journey_email",
        "get_journey",
        "get_journey_email",
        "list_journeys",
        "test_journey_email",
        "update_journey_email",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

  "action": "activate_journey_email",

  "doc": "An email with no subject or no body is refused with 422. Activating an active email changes nothing. Confirm with the person before calling it.",
  "readonly": false,
  "idempotent": true,
  "destructive": true,
  "params": [
    {
      "name": "trigger",
      "in": "path",
      "required": true,
      "description": "The journey's trigger: subscriber_confirmed or subscriber_unsubscribed",
      "schema": {
        "description": "The journey's trigger: subscriber_confirmed or subscriber_unsubscribed",
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "email_id",
      "in": "path",
      "required": true,
      "description": "The email's ID (from its journey)",
      "schema": {
        "description": "The email's ID (from its journey)",
        "type": "string"
      }
    }
  ]
}

        "type": "integer"
      },

        "description": "Subject",
        "type": "string"
      },
      "summary": {
        "description": "The writer's own line about the email, shown by an inbox beside the subject",

    },
    "required": [
      "subject"
    ],
    "type": "object"
  }
}

==== TOOL mailpiece_settings ====
title: Mailpiece Settings
Mailpiece settings: the newsletter's own configuration, each part a record of its own. Its name, description and language; the handle it answers at; who its mail is from; where its embedded subscription form sends a person back to; the code people join its team with; and whether the signed-in admin is emailed about new subscribers. Admins only.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- get_handle (RO): Get the handle the newsletter answers at beside its number, null while it has none
- get_join_code (RO): Get the code people join the newsletter's team with, its link, and how often it has been used
- get_newsletter (RO): Get the newsletter's name, description and language
- get_notifications (RO): Get whether the signed-in admin is emailed when someone confirms a subscription
- get_sending (RO): Get who the newsletter's mail is from and how it leaves: from name, from address, reply-to and transport
- get_subscribe_form (RO): Get where the embedded subscription form sends a person back to
- remove_sending_relay (destructive): Remove the relay and its token; the newsletter sends nothing until a transport is set again. This cannot be undone.
- remove_sending_smtp (destructive): Remove the SMTP server and its password; the newsletter sends nothing until a transport is set again. This cannot be undone.
- reset_join_code (destructive): Retire the join code and issue a new one, used no times; the old code and every link carrying it stop working. This cannot be undone.
- update_handle (destructive): Change the newsletter's handle, or clear it so the newsletter answers at its number alone. Every link already mailed with the old handle stops working. This cannot be undone.
- update_join_code: Change how many times the join code can be used
- update_newsletter: Change the newsletter's name, description or language; only what is passed changes
- update_notifications: Set whether the signed-in admin is emailed when someone confirms a subscription
- update_sending: Change who the newsletter's mail is from; only what is passed changes
- update_sending_relay: Send the newsletter's mail through a relay; replaces an SMTP server if one was set
- update_sending_smtp: Send the newsletter's mail through an SMTP server; replaces a relay if one was set
- update_subscribe_form: Set where the embedded subscription form sends a person back to
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "get_handle",
        "get_join_code",
        "get_newsletter",
        "get_notifications",
        "get_sending",
        "get_subscribe_form",
        "remove_sending_relay",
        "remove_sending_smtp",
        "reset_join_code",
        "update_handle",
        "update_join_code",
        "update_newsletter",
        "update_notifications",
        "update_sending",
        "update_sending_relay",
        "update_sending_smtp",
        "update_subscribe_form",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}
---- describe get_handle ----
{
  "action": "get_handle",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/account/handle",
  "summary": "Get the handle the newsletter answers at beside its number, null while it has none",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false
}
---- describe get_join_code ----
{
  "action": "get_join_code",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/account/join_code",
  "summary": "Get the code people join the newsletter's team with, its link, and how often it has been used",
  "doc": "active is false once usage_count has reached usage_limit.",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false
}
---- describe get_newsletter ----
{
  "action": "get_newsletter",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/account/newsletter",
  "summary": "Get the newsletter's name, description and language",
  "doc": "description is the text alone and description_html what was written. avatar_url is there only when the newsletter has an avatar.",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false
}
---- describe get_notifications ----
{
  "action": "get_notifications",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/notifications/settings",
  "summary": "Get whether the signed-in admin is emailed when someone confirms a subscription",
  "doc": "It is the token's own user's setting, on until switched off.",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false
}
---- describe get_sending ----
{
  "action": "get_sending",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/account/sending",
  "summary": "Get who the newsletter's mail is from and how it leaves: from name, from address, reply-to and transport",
  "doc": "A newsletter mails nothing until it has a from name, a from address and a transport. transport is null, relay or smtp, with the relay and SMTP settings beside it. The relay token and the SMTP password are never returned.",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false
}
---- describe get_subscribe_form ----
{
  "action": "get_subscribe_form",
  "method": "GET",
  "path": "/account/subscribe_form",
  "summary": "Get where the embedded subscription form sends a person back to",
  "readonly": true,
  "idempotent": false,
  "destructive": false
}

==== TOOL mailpiece_users ====
title: Mailpiece Users
Mailpiece users: the signed-in person's own user on the newsletter. A user reaches only their own profile: anyone else's is a 404. The identity tool shows your user's ID on each account.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- get_user (RO): Get your own user: name, role, email address
- update_user: Change your own name
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "get_user",
        "update_user",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

==== TOOL mailpiece_posts ====
title: Mailpiece Posts
A newsletter's posts: drafts, their release to the web and to the list of subscribers, and the links and earlier versions a post keeps. Admins only. A post is published once and sent once; a scheduled post is still a draft. Mailing the list cannot be undone: never deliver, or schedule a delivery, unless the person asked for exactly that.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- create_post: Write a draft. Nothing is published or mailed.
- delete_post (destructive): Delete a post in any state, with its revisions, deliveries and links: the links in an issue already mailed stop answering. This cannot be undone.
- deliver_post (destructive): Mail a post now to every active subscriber, publishing it first if it is a draft. This cannot be undone.
- get_post (RO): Get a post in any state
- get_post_revision (RO): Get one earlier version of a post, with its title and text
- list_post_links (RO): List the links a post's issue was mailed with
- list_post_revisions (RO): List a post's earlier versions, oldest first, without their text
- list_posts (RO): List what is ahead: the drafts, newest first, then the scheduled posts, soonest first
- list_published_posts (RO, paginated): List the posts published and not mailed, newest first
- list_sent_posts (RO, paginated): List the posts mailed to the list, newest first
- publish_post: Give a post its page, mailing nobody
- relist_post: Show a published post that is on the web in the archive and the feed (visibility listed)
- schedule_post: Set when a draft is released by itself; scheduling again moves the time. A scheduled delivery mails every active subscriber when it runs, and that mail cannot be taken back; unschedule_post stops it before then.
- test_post (destructive): Mail a test of a post as it stands to one address. The list is not mailed and the post does not change, but the test is real mail. This cannot be undone.
- unlist_post: Keep a published post's page and take it out of the archive and the feed (visibility unlisted)
- unpublish_post: Take a post's page down
- unschedule_post: Cancel a draft's schedule; it stays a draft
- update_post: Edit a post, changing only what is sent
- update_post_link: Correct where a mailed link sends a reader from now on; the email already sent keeps its text
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "create_post",
        "delete_post",
        "deliver_post",
        "get_post",
        "get_post_revision",
        "list_post_links",
        "list_post_revisions",
        "list_posts",
        "list_published_posts",
        "list_sent_posts",
        "publish_post",
        "relist_post",
        "schedule_post",
        "test_post",
        "unlist_post",
        "unpublish_post",
        "unschedule_post",
        "update_post",
        "update_post_link",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

==== TOOL mailpiece_search ====
title: Mailpiece Search
Search a newsletter: the posts and the subscribers a query matches. Admins only.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- search (RO, paginated): Find the posts and the subscribers matching a query, newest first

==== TOOL mailpiece_subscribers ====
title: Mailpiece Subscribers
Mailpiece subscribers: the people on the newsletter's list. A subscriber's status is one of, read in this order: bounced (the mail server stopped delivering to the address), deactivated (an admin stopped it), unsubscribed (the person left), confirmed, or unconfirmed (it has not answered its confirmation yet). Only a confirmed subscriber is mailed. Only the person undoes an unsubscribe or a bounce, by subscribing again from the public form and confirming from the link mailed to them: no action here does it for them. Admins only.

Gateway tool: call with {"action": "...", "params": {...}}.
Call {"action": "describe", "params": {"action": "NAME"}} for an action's full parameter schema.

ACTIONS (RO = read-only):
- activate_subscriber: Resume a subscriber an admin stopped. It undoes neither an unsubscribe nor a bounce.
- bounce_subscriber (destructive): Mark a subscriber bounced, so it is no longer mailed; only the person undoes it, by subscribing again. This cannot be undone.
- bounce_subscriber_address (destructive): Mark bounced the subscriber with an address, so it is no longer mailed; only the person undoes it, by subscribing again. This cannot be undone.
- create_subscriber: Add one address to the list, already confirmed: no confirmation is mailed. Refused for an address that unsubscribed, bounced or was stopped.
- deactivate_subscriber: Stop mailing a subscriber, keeping it and its history; activate_subscriber resumes it.
- delete_subscriber (destructive): Delete a subscriber for good, with its deliveries and journey history. This cannot be undone.
- get_subscriber (RO, paginated): Show a subscriber with the issues mailed to it, newest first
- list_bounced_subscribers (RO, paginated): List the subscribers the mail server stopped delivering to, most recently bounced first
- list_deactivated_subscribers (RO, paginated): List the subscribers an admin stopped, most recently stopped first
- list_subscribers (RO, paginated): List the confirmed subscribers, the people an issue is mailed to, newest first
- list_unconfirmed_subscribers (RO, paginated): List the subscribers that have not answered their confirmation yet, newest first
- list_unsubscribed_subscribers (RO, paginated): List the subscribers that left, most recently unsubscribed first
---- input schema ----
{
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "properties": {
    "action": {
      "enum": [
        "activate_subscriber",
        "bounce_subscriber",
        "bounce_subscriber_address",
        "create_subscriber",
        "deactivate_subscriber",
        "delete_subscriber",
        "get_subscriber",
        "list_bounced_subscribers",
        "list_deactivated_subscribers",
        "list_subscribers",
        "list_unconfirmed_subscribers",
        "list_unsubscribed_subscribers",
        "describe"
      ],
      "type": "string"
    },
    "params": {
      "description": "Parameters for the action. Call describe for the action's schema.",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "action"
  ],
  "type": "object"
}

  "doc": "Reverses deactivate_subscriber and nothing else: the subscriber goes back to the state it was in, confirmed and mailed again or still unconfirmed. The app answers 201 only when it resumed the person and 200 when it changed nothing. The result here is the subscriber either way, without the status: one that was not stopped comes back unchanged, so read its status with get_subscriber first to tell the two apart.",
  "readonly": false,
  "idempotent": true,

  "params": [
